title: How to make story discovery and sourcing faster: a guide for journalists on Mac
metaTitle: How to make story discovery and sourcing faster for journalists on Mac
description: Learn how journalists find stories efficiently on Mac. Discover tools for sourcing, research management, and workflow fixes to reduce burnout and improve accuracy.
targetKeyword: how to make story discovery and sourcing faster
intro: Journalists find stories by building networks, monitoring beats, and digging into public records. You can make this process faster by using a structured research database and a Mac-based assistant to manage your context.
tldr: Use a local-first document store like DEVONthink to keep your research searchable and secure.
Centralize your notes in an app like Obsidian to maintain links between sources.
Use Lazur to keep your research context accessible while you jump between apps.
Verify every claim by grounding your AI research in specific, trusted documents.
Schedule dedicated research blocks to avoid the trap of constant email checking.

stats.label: journalists finding only half of pitches relevant

blocks.text: The core of your job is finding the truth. But the volume of incoming information is massive. You get hundreds of emails, social media mentions, and press releases every day. Most of it is noise. Filtering this noise takes hours. When you are under pressure to file multiple stories a week, you have less time to dig deep. This leads to surface-level reporting and potential errors.

When you cannot find a source quickly, you lose time. You spend your day switching between Gmail, Slack, and your browser. Every switch costs mental energy. You might miss a lead because it was buried in a thread you did not check. Worse, you might misinterpret data because you did not have time to verify it against primary sources.

items: Create a local database. Use DEVONthink or a similar tool to store PDFs and notes. This keeps your research on your Mac, not on a server where it might be exposed.
Use citation managers. Zotero is free and helps you track where your information came from. This builds a trail of evidence for every story.
Ground your research. If you use AI to summarize documents, make sure you upload the specific file. Do not rely on general web knowledge.
Set strict boundaries. Use the Focus mode on your Mac to block notifications for two hours while you research.
Organize your browser. Use OneTab to collapse your open tabs into a list. This saves memory and keeps your workspace clean.

blocks.text: Lazur lives in the notch of your Mac. It sees what you see. You can hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about a document you are looking at. It helps you keep track of your research without leaving your writing app.

rows: Review key beats and scan top sources
Organize notes and prepare for tomorrow

faq.question: Is Lazur safe for sensitive source information?
faq.answer: Lazur only sees your screen when you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots are not stored. They are sent to AI providers to answer your request and then discarded.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with my existing writing apps?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any app on your Mac. You can ask it to help you with research in Word, Google Docs, or any other editor.

faq.question: Can Lazur write my articles for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is designed to assist with research, synthesis, and workflow. You must write your own stories to ensure accuracy and voice.

costs.title: Cognitive load
costs.text: Constant context switching between email, Slack, and research tabs drains your mental energy.

costs.title: Accuracy risks
costs.text: Rushed deadlines often mean less time to verify facts, leading to potential errors in your reporting.

costs.title: Burnout
costs.text: The pressure to file multiple stories daily while filtering through irrelevant pitches causes chronic stress.

causes.title: Information overload
causes.text: Most pitches are irrelevant, forcing you to spend valuable time filtering through noise.

causes.title: Resource depletion
causes.text: Many newsrooms have cut fact-checking roles, leaving the entire burden of verification on you.

causes.title: Skill gaps
causes.text: Interpreting complex academic studies or statistics without formal training is a common challenge.

fixes.title: Local-first storage
fixes.text: Use tools like DEVONthink to keep your research files searchable and secure on your Mac.

fixes.title: Structured note-taking
fixes.text: Use an app like Obsidian to link your sources and build a persistent knowledge base.

fixes.title: Time blocking
fixes.text: Dedicate specific hours to research to avoid the constant distraction of checking email.

plan.label: Morning
plan.title: Clear the noise
plan.text: Spend 30 minutes scanning your inbox and flagging leads. Close your mail app immediately after.

plan.label: Mid-morning
plan.title: Deep research
plan.text: Open your research database. Use your Mac to find primary sources. Do not check Slack.

plan.label: Afternoon
plan.title: Draft and verify
plan.text: Write your story. Use Lazur to check your notes or look up specific facts without breaking your flow.
